thread.title_full: Inside St. Pete mayor's Tropicana Field redevelopment picks - NewsBreak

author: Kathryn Varn
title: Inside St. Pete mayor's Tropicana Field redevelopment picks - NewsBreak
text:
By Kathryn Varn ,
8 hours ago
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected Blake Investment Partners to redevelop Tropicana Field , several news outlets reported.
Why it matters: It's a major step forward for the city's most consequential piece of land and for Welch's campaign promise to remake the Historic Gas Plant District .
But the issue is far from settled. Any plans are subject to City Council approval, and the results of the upcoming mayoral election could upend the process. Zoom in: Blake's proposal , called The Burg Bid, offers the city $275 million in cash for 58 acres of the Trop site. That's the highest offer of his competitors, and the city would retain ownership of about a third of the land.
The proposal includes plans to build more than 3,600 income-restricted housing units, with half planned for the district and the remaining units scattered throughout the city. A 13-acre park would be named after a Gas Plant descendant and feature a "Museum Row" anchored by the Woodson African American Museum of Florida. Local artists Chad Mize and Mark Aeling would lead a nearby Museum of Public Art. The proposal also calls for hotels, a small business incubator and a workforce training center, plus a Legacy Link walking trail that would connect The Deuces to downtown. Along with the Blake bid, Welch also selected a pitch from the Pinellas County Housing Authority to build 80 affordable apartments for seniors on a half-acre of the 86-acre property, the Tampa Bay Times reported .
Between the lines: City spokesperson Samantha Bequer did not confirm the mayor's picks to Axios or other media . City Council members either did not respond or declined to comment to Axios.
Thompson Whitney Blake, the St. Pete native and investor who spearheaded the Blake Investment Partners proposal, also did not return requests for comment. The intrigue: Peter Schorsch, a local political operative and the publisher of FloridaPolitics.com , scooped Welch's announcement Tuesday night at a City Council candidate forum organized by Suncoast Tiger Bay.
Schorsch's wife, Michelle Todd Schorsch, is managing the mayoral campaign of one of Welch's opponents , former Gov. and U.S. Rep. Charlie Crist. What's next: Welch is set to announce his selections at a news conference at 9am Thursday at Campbell Park. It will be livestreamed on the city's Facebook page .
Welch's picks will be vetted by the Community Benefits Advisory Council , a resident panel that will hold two meetings in July, including one open to the public to offer feedback. Welch will then begin negotiating the terms of the project, which will go before the City Council for approval.
